content.title: About
content.content: Baby spinach consists of tender young leaves of the annual plant Spinacia oleracea. It is harvested early in the growth cycle when the leaves are small, soft, and bright green. The vegetable is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants, and has a mild, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach belongs to the Amaranthaceae family and is one of the oldest cultivated leafy greens.
Nitrate levels can be high in spinach, especially when grown in heated greenhouses, but they decrease with proper storage and cooking.
In the 19th century, American physician Paul Betther promoted spinach for strength, inspiring the “Popeye” comic character.
Baby spinach is commonly used raw in salads, smoothies, and as a garnish for fish and meat dishes.
Commercial production in Russia began in the 1990s, making it available year‑round.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: 100 g of baby spinach provides over 500 µg of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and folate
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, while folate supports cell division and fetal development during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related changes and UV damage.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Spinach contains about 2.9 g of protein per 100 g and is low in calories, making it diet‑friendly.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in spinach aids intestinal function and promotes satiety.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: Oxalates may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals; moderate intake is advised.

items.title: Nitrates
items.content: Elevated nitrate levels can be a concern for infants; thorough washing and cooking are recommended.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience spinach allergy with skin rashes or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baby spinach can be eaten raw in salads, blended into smoothies, used as a topping for wraps and sandwiches, or quickly sautéed with garlic. Because the leaves wilt rapidly, they are added at the end of cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store spinach in the refrigerator in a bag with a small amount of moisture or in a container lined with a paper towel. Use within 3‑5 days. Freezing changes the texture but retains most nutrients.
